correctionsToTheDispatchPremise.measured: ORIGINAL (WRONG) DIAGNOSIS: this lane treated not_specified uniformly as an honest-absence sentinel per table-types.d.ts's own documented contract ('Set true when the value is the NOT_SPECIFIED sentinel'), and reported Austin's 218,021-parcel zero-value-cell outcome as a corpus completeness gap. CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (doc-repo-4a, independently re-verified by this lane against the live corpus, not taken on the peer's word): not_specified is a FLAG-SEMANTICS DEFECT, not an absence marker, for the majority of its real occurrences. Peer's file-based audit (scratchpad/not_specified_audit.py, corpus repo main b8020c8b) of all 548 (district x {max_height_ft, max_lot_coverage_pct}) slots found 329 CONTRADICTION (a real transcribed value co-occurring with the flag), 219 CLEAN_VALUE, and ZERO HONEST_ABSENCE -- the flag never once, across 548 slots, sits on an actually-missing value. This lane independently re-verified the Austin case directly against the live corpus file: SF-1/SF-3/MF-6 all carry real, specific values (35ft/35%, 35ft/40%, 90ft/70%) on the flagged fields, at confidence 0.6, versus confidence 0.7 on the ADJACENT, UNFLAGGED front_ft field in the same district record -- a modest confidence discount, not an absence signal -- and the quote itself states verbatim that '25-2-492 site-development table: SF-1 row provides the stated base-yard, height, building-coverage, and impervious-cover values,' directly asserting the value IS stated in the source ordinance. Bastrop's case (this lane's original clean example) remains genuinely different: its quote explicitly disclaims the metric ('a separate lot-coverage percentage is not modeled as a distinct scalar here') and its raw value is a literal 0 placeholder -- the flag's DOCUMENTED meaning may be correct for Bastrop-shaped entries specifically while being wrong for Austin-shaped ones. Blast radius per the peer's audit: 329 contradictions across 22 of 29 jurisdictions (worst: san-antonio-tx 42/0, leander-tx 34/0, liberty-hill-tx 28/0, austin-tx 18/0, cedar-park-tx 25/7, belton-tx 24/20).
correctionsToTheDispatchPremise.consequence: THIS LANE'S ALREADY-APPLIED PRODUCTION WRITE IS AFFECTED: the full --apply run wrote absent-verified for maxHeightFt/maxLotCoveragePct (and the maxFootprintSqFt cells that inherit from them) on every not_specified-flagged field-slot this job's corpus lookup encountered, including the majority-CONTRADICTION population the peer's audit identifies. Per ENFORCEMENT.md's own stronger framing (quoted by the peer): 'absent-verified is a claim that something looked; writing it where nothing looked is a lie that passes every check' -- here something DID look, found a cited value, and the cell was still written absent. This is wrong in a KNOWN direction (conservative: a real value was withheld, not fabricated), which the peer correctly notes is better than wrong in an unknown one, but it is still wrong and at real scale.
correctionsToTheDispatchPremise.disposition: NOT bulk-flipped by this lane -- per the peer's own explicit instruction, the correct resolution is a ruling from the corpus owner (property seat) on what not_specified actually means and how the two shapes (Bastrop-style genuine absence vs Austin-style confidence-discounted real value) should be told apart mechanically, followed by a dedicated remediation lane. The peer is routing this to the operator now as a corpus-owner ruling plus a remediation-lane request. This close records precisely which cells this lane's own run affected (see liveVerification.correctionAfterApply below) so that remediation lane knows exactly what to undo without re-deriving it.

fleetMemoryScratch.text: When a dispatch's own STANDING FACTS name only ONE dependency for a set of rails, check each rail's ACTUAL data requirement independently rather than assuming they share one dependency chain -- three of this lane's four rails needed zoningDistrict, but parcelAreaSqFt (pure geometry) did not, and treating it as bundled would have withheld a real, immediately-available value from every deferred parcel.

A corpus field's own documented sentinel flag (not_specified) can appear on MULTIPLE distinct fields with different real-world rates (73% for max_lot_coverage_pct, 47% for max_height_ft) -- write the field-gating logic once, generically, and verify EACH field's own rate empirically rather than assuming a pattern found on one field doesn't apply to a sibling field. This job's own first-draft doc comment got this wrong for max_height_ft and was caught only by writing a real test against live corpus data.

A pure, DB-free, dependency-free (or public-npm-only) geometry/math module in a sibling repo is legitimately portable-and-citable even when its surrounding business logic (routing, live data fetches) is not -- but a peer catching that the port's OUTPUT has nowhere honest to land (per an existing program-wide ruling) should stop the port before it's written, not after. Citing the files/commit for a future lane costs nothing; building an engine whose output cannot ship is a dormant mechanism that creates pressure to find somewhere to put it.

Re-verify a sibling PR's cloudbuild substitution values before copying them into a new config -- S1's own pin was already stale within 24 hours (six _LDT_SHA bumps documented in that program's own register) because of unrelated churn in a completely different job's dependency. A new job with zero actual dependency on the pinned repo should use the Dockerfile's own current default, not inherit a sibling's soon-to-be-stale snapshot.
